Name: untitled-1: evolution sliding puzzle

VisualLanguage.rendering: flat colour cartoon with a black outline and one darker shade step per colour
VisualLanguage.mood: friendly, playful, a little funny; every creature looks happy to evolve
VisualLanguage.world: a cartoon history of life, from the sea to the land

rules: Each colour is one flat area. Shade with the darker colour of the same family, as one hard-edged step, never a gradient.
Outline every creature in black $00, thick and even.
Eyes are large: a white area with a black pupil, big enough to stay white at 48 pixels across.

LineAndShape.outline: black, thick, about 1/24 of the creature's width
LineAndShape.shapes: large, simple, rounded; a strong silhouette that is clear when the creature is the size of a thumbnail
LineAndShape.proportions: chibi: a big head and a small body, so the face is easy to see

SubjectLanguage.creatures: Each creature is one character with a face that shows a happy, curious expression. Each is clearly different in shape and main colour from the creatures before and after it in the chain.
SubjectLanguage.scale: Every creature fills the frame the same way, whatever its real size: a microbe is as large on the tile as a dinosaur.

BackgroundPolicy.default: transparent; the program draws the board square behind the creature

TypographyPolicy.default: No words, letters, numbers or pseudo-text.

CompositionPolicy.sprite: One creature, centred, the whole body inside the frame, with even padding of about one tenth of the frame on every side. Three-quarter front view, facing the viewer.

QualityRules: The creature reads clearly as a silhouette.
No detail smaller than the minimum feature size.
All eleven creatures look like one family of characters drawn by the same artist.

ApprovedSamples.use: the owner-approved style for every creature: thick black outline, flat colour with one darker shade step, big white eyes with black pupils, chibi proportions, cheerful open-mouth smile, the same scale and padding
